questions.q: The lesson's requirements.txt pinned scikit-learn and pandas but not NumPy, and training crashed on a fresh install. What was the underlying problem?
options: NumPy cannot be installed with pip
pip installed the newest NumPy, which was too new for the pinned pandas build, because transitive dependencies were not pinned
The virtual environment was activated incorrectly
scikit-learn 1.1.2 does not support Python
questions.explain: Libraries usually declare only minimum versions of their own dependencies, so unpinned transitive packages can drift to incompatible releases.

questions.q: What is the difference between requirements.txt and requirements.lock in this lesson?
options: The lock file is the short list written by hand; requirements.txt is generated
They are identical and only one is needed
requirements.txt lists the libraries you chose; the lock file is tool-generated and lists every installed package at an exact version
The lock file is only for conda users
questions.explain: The requirements file is your short, readable intent; the lock file is the full exact record produced by pip freeze or a lock tool.

questions.q: Why did the lesson build a brand-new environment from the lock file and diff its pip freeze against it?
options: A lock file that has never been rebuilt from scratch is only an untested guess, so this proves it reproduces the environment
Because pip freeze cannot be run twice
To make training run faster
To upgrade every package to the latest release
questions.explain: Rebuilding and comparing shows the lock is complete; the empty diff and the same 0.768 accuracy confirmed it.

questions.q: A churn model saved under scikit-learn 1.1.2 was loaded under 1.6.1. What happened?
options: It loaded silently and predicted identically
The file was automatically upgraded to the new version
Loading was refused with a permissions error
Version warnings appeared on load and predict_proba then failed with an AttributeError
questions.explain: A joblib file is a pickle that expects matching library code. Mismatches can fail loudly, or worse, quietly change predictions.

questions.q: Which practice best protects a project from environment drift?
options: Installing the latest version of every package before each run
Keeping one shared global Python installation for all projects
Committing the .venv folder to Git
One virtual environment per project, a lock file, a from-scratch rebuild check, and a saved version fingerprint next to each model
questions.explain: Isolate, lock, verify and record. The .venv folder itself is machine-specific and stays out of Git.
